title: Design MDG for an automotive multi-plant rollout
prompt: An automotive group introduces one central MDG hub for Material and Supplier data across 12 plants and 7 consuming systems. Plants have local planning and warehouse requirements, while legal identity and supplier bank data must be centrally controlled. Design the governance, replication, migration and operating model.
expected_points: separate global Material identity from plant, sales, valuation, warehouse and quality grains
separate BP core identity from supplier company-code and purchasing-organization behavior
define CR patterns for create, organizational extension, sensitive change and mass change
assign business ownership and approval rights by grain instead of by screen
define validation/derivation and BRFplus routing responsibilities separately
define DRF replication models, target filters, identity/key mapping and target acceptance evidence
design initial-load-to-delta cut-off and source-target reconciliation
define rollback/recovery for activation and replication failures
prove readiness with real MRP, purchasing, EWM or sales transactions in representative plants
define operational metrics, exception ownership and hypercare exit criteria
follow_up_questions: Would every plant use the same change-request type?
How do you prevent a local plant from changing global product identity?
What proves that the initial load and first delta have no gap?
Which attributes would you treat as high-risk for supplier governance?
red_flags: uses one global workflow for every change
counts only Material or BP root records in migration
lets local teams overwrite shared identity without ownership rules
declares success when DRF messages are green

title: Material is active but one plant cannot plan it
prompt: A Material change request is approved and active. Sales can use the product, but MRP in one plant plans it incorrectly and EWM later rejects the product context. Trace the first wrong boundary without manually fixing the target systems.
expected_points: freeze Material identity, plant, change request, activation version and affected target systems
separate global Material identity from plant and warehouse grains
inspect plant entities and required MRP/ATP/purchasing/quality/work-scheduling data rather than only MATERIAL root
prove whether the expected plant slice is active
trace DRF selection, filters, outbound payload, identity mapping and target acceptance
separate EWM rejection from the original MRP symptom if they fail at different boundaries
compare a working plant with the failing plant using effective data and configuration
correct the earliest wrong governed state and retest MRP and warehouse execution
follow_up_questions: What evidence proves the issue is not a global Material problem?
When would replay be the wrong recovery action?
How would you detect similar incomplete plant extensions before go-live?
red_flags: edits the EWM product locally first
assumes active root means all organizational slices are complete
replays all replication without checking current source and target state

title: Merge duplicate suppliers without losing identity control
prompt: Two active supplier BPs appear to represent the same legal company. Both have purchasing history, different local addresses and different external IDs in connected systems. A matching score is high. Decide whether and how to consolidate them.
expected_points: treat matching score as evidence rather than merge authority
inspect strong identity evidence, ambiguous attributes, previous match decisions and transaction history
define review band and accountable identity owner
separate matching decision from survivorship/value-precedence decision
apply source, recency, completeness or domain rules by table/field rather than one global winner
record manual overrides and provenance
choose duplicate strategy only after understanding downstream transaction and key-mapping behavior
preserve source-to-surviving-identity mapping and replacement semantics
replicate/reconcile identity changes to consumers and validate purchasing/payment behavior
retain rollback or controlled recovery options where technically possible
follow_up_questions: When is Remove Duplicates too risky?
Would the newest address always win?
How do you handle a trusted legal source and a different trusted procurement source?
red_flags: automatically merges because score is high
chooses the row with most populated fields as golden record
deletes one supplier before checking transaction history
ignores key mapping and downstream identities

title: Recover MDG replication after a target outage
prompt: A target ERP system was unavailable for two hours. MDG continued activating Business Partner and Material changes. Some messages failed, some timed out, and later changes may have succeeded. Design the recovery without overwriting newer target truth or creating duplicates.
expected_points: define affected source objects, target, time window and stable correlation identities
prove current active source state and distinguish historical failed payloads from current truth
classify failures into selection, payload, transport, target semantic rejection, identity mapping or downstream consumption
check whether the target persisted any timed-out attempts
assess idempotency, ordering and duplicate behavior before replay
prefer rebuilding from current active truth when historical payload is stale
replay only controlled populations with source-target reconciliation
check key mapping before resolving identity-related failures
measure selected, sent, accepted, rejected, replayed and unresolved objects
prove business consumer use after technical recovery
follow_up_questions: When should you replay the old message versus rebuild from active data?
How do you prove that a timeout did not already persist the object?
What changes if updates must be processed in order?
red_flags: uses middleware delivery status as final success
repairs IDs manually without checking mapping collisions
